title: Single-GPU forward + backward
scope: One Qwen-shaped dense layer · BF16 · sequence 4096

verification.label: Measured single-H100 dense training step
verification.implementation: Explicit Qwen-shaped GQA using PyTorch Flash SDPA, dense SwiGLU, and AdamW foreach
verification.workload: Hidden 4096, 64 query heads, 4 KV heads, head dimension 128, dense intermediate 12288, batch 1, sequence 4096, BF16
verification.measurement: 16.204 ms CUDA-event wall time; 15.093 ms dependency-packed rank-0 GPU busy timeline shown
verification.timeline: Measured GPU busy durations packed without CPU launch gaps; backward includes activation gradI and optimizer is a real AdamW step.

description: This onboarding challenge intentionally stays high-level: attention forward, MLP forward, a scalar loss, the two reverse-mode blocks, and an optimizer step.

The measured attention contains RMSNorm, Q/K/V projections, FlashAttention, and the output projection. The measured MLP contains RMSNorm and all three dense SwiGLU projections. Those kernels are aggregated so the first exercise teaches dependencies rather than kernel trivia.

The benchmark uses a mean-squared activation loss over synthetic hidden states. This keeps the loss self-contained; the dependency order is the same as a language-model loss, but its duration must not be interpreted as cross-entropy timing.
